blueprint.name: Smart Home Battery
blueprint.description: Generic Home Assistant blueprint for up to four batteries. It allocates discharge from house demand, can trigger opportunistic charging during real export, pauses normal target control during off-peak periods so external automations can manage overnight charging, and writes a signed power target for each battery into a numeric entity, with optional custom actions for integrations that need a separate mode switch.
message.invalid_sensor: House power sensor {{ house_power_sensor }} is unavailable or not numeric.
message.small_delta_skipped: House power sensor delta below trigger threshold:
message.off_peak_actions_only: Off-peak period active: the blueprint stops without running any action.
trace.stop_small_delta: Stop on small house power delta
validation.no_target_entity.suffix: is enabled by its state of charge sensor, but no Target power entity is configured. Add a `number` or `input_number` entity, or clear the state of charge sensor to disable this battery slot.
validation.no_power.suffix: has a target power entity configured, but both maximum power limits are set to 0 W. Set a non-zero Maximum discharge power or Maximum charge power to make this slot usable.
input.house_power_sensor.name: House power sensor
input.house_power_sensor.description: Main house power sensor. This selector only shows power sensors. Use a signed sensor in watts with positive values for import and negative values for export.
input.off_peak_entities.name: Active off-peak entities
input.off_peak_entities.description: Optional entities that turn on during off-peak periods. If at least one selected entity stays on for 15 seconds, the blueprint stops immediately without running actions or writing targets, so external automations can fully manage overnight charging. Leaving on is handled immediately.
input.battery.soc_sensor.name: State of charge sensor
input.battery.soc_sensor.description: Leave empty to ignore this battery slot. Otherwise, this selector only shows battery sensors that report a charge percentage, and the chosen sensor enables the slot. An enabled slot must also expose a numeric target entity and at least one non-zero power limit.
input.battery.max_discharge_w.name: Maximum discharge power
input.battery.max_discharge_w.descriptio: Manual discharge limit used by the allocator for this battery.
input.battery.min_discharge_soc_pct.name: Minimum state of charge for discharge
input.battery.min_discharge_soc_pct.desc: Minimum state of charge required before this battery can be assigned discharge power. If the battery is below this threshold, the blueprint removes it from discharge allocation and writes 0 if it still has an active discharge target.
input.battery.max_charge_w.name: Maximum charge power
input.battery.max_charge_w.description: Manual charge limit used by the allocator for opportunistic charging from real export. When a solar-connected battery is full, this limit is used to absorb as much raw export as possible. Set to 0 if this battery must never be charged by the blueprint.
input.battery.cooldown_seconds.name: Command cooldown
input.battery.cooldown_seconds.descripti: Minimum delay between two active target updates for this battery. A short cooldown makes the battery available to absorb residual changes and recover export before slower batteries. A longer cooldown keeps the target steadier. Set it to 0 to disable the delay entirely. Writing `0` can still happen immediately so the blueprint can stop a battery for safety. The shortest-cooldown charge-capable battery can restart from `0` immediately when the raw house meter confirms matching import or export, but during normal import it waits if a higher-SoC-margin battery still has discharge headroom, unless the import is strong. It can absorb the existing charge target plus remaining raw export when a solar-connected battery is full, and taper that charge target across short import rebounds instead of dropping directly to `0`. If that charge-capable battery is still discharging during this full-solar overflow, the blueprint stops it at `0 W` first, then lets it charge after it returns to the discharge deadband. Slower batteries wait for their cooldown before restarting from `0`, while raw export can still reduce an active discharge target before the cooldown expires.
input.battery.target_power_entity.name: Target power entity
input.battery.target_power_entity.descri: The `number` or `input_number` entity written by the blueprint. The target is signed in watts: positive for discharge, negative for charge, `0` for stop. If this battery should charge, the selected entity must accept negative values.
input.battery.target_power_uses_absolute: Enable this when the target entity expects a positive power magnitude for both charge and discharge. The blueprint keeps an internal signed target, writes the absolute value to this entity, and relies on charge/discharge actions to select the battery direction. When telemetry does not confirm the requested direction, those direction actions are retried so a stale charge mode cannot block discharge.
Enable this only for a battery directly connected to solar panels that may keep outputting their production when it is full despite a 0 target. When enabled, physical discharge at a zero target is treated as forced solar output only while the SoC is at least 99%.
input.battery.actual_power_sensor.name: Actual power sensor
input.battery.actual_power_sensor.descri: Optional power sensor that reports the battery's real output in watts. The allocator still uses the target entity and the house meter as its primary control loop. After the response grace period, only a fresh reading is used as a guardrail to avoid counting a battery as real supply when it is no longer delivering. Old or stale telemetry does not prevent an idle battery from starting and does not keep an active battery out of extra discharge allocation by itself; the allocator falls back to the commanded target until a fresh reading returns.
input.battery.discharge_actions.name: Discharge actions
input.battery.discharge_actions.descript: Optional custom actions executed when this battery should actively discharge, and again when it should stop but still reports physical discharge outside off-peak periods. They run on every active discharge target update outside off-peak periods. Variables such as battery_slot, battery_soc, target_power_w, target_discharge_w, target_charge_w, house_power_w, import_need_w and export_surplus_w are available inside these actions; target variables are initialized globally and then overwritten with the current slot values before this sequence runs.
input.battery.charge_actions.name: Charge actions
input.battery.charge_actions.description: Optional custom actions executed when this battery should actively charge from surplus export, and again when it should stop but still reports physical charge. They run on every active charge target update outside off-peak periods. Variables such as battery_slot, battery_soc, target_power_w, target_discharge_w, target_charge_w, house_power_w, import_need_w and export_surplus_w are available inside these actions; target variables are initialized globally and then overwritten with the current slot values before this sequence runs.
